subject: Gaussian Process modelling of an intercept+effect model with noisy replicates

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Gaussian Process modelling of an intercept+effect model with noisy replicates
parts:
Hi folks,

I've been trying to apply Gaussian Process models to data typical of my research domain for a while, and I think I've got it figured out now. 

Here's a gist with R & stan code for a demonstration: https://gist.github.com/mike-lawrence/9ad22f38e53b575586ea238bf8388a2a

I've tried to comment both data-generation & model code thoroughly to walk you through the scenario.

The general idea is that the outcome Y is observed on a grid of values of X under two conditions. I want to model the possibly-non-linear functions of Y as a function of X in each condition, which I achieve by defining an "intercept" GP and "effect" GP and combining these to get two condition functions. Finally, because I have lots of observations per X per condition, I model these replicates as having random Gaussian deviations from their condition function.

The only issue that I seem to have left is that the model appears to have some numerical issues unless jitter is added to the GPs. That is, note that the model has a data variable called "fudge". If you set this to something very small, like 1e-7, the model takes a long time to sample but the resulting posteriors on both functions are nice and smooth. In contrast, if you set this to something larger like 1e-3, the model samples quickly but the posteriors on both functions are very noisy seeming.

I know that there is typically jitter added to a GP (usually called sigma), but it seemed unwise to do so in this case because I already add noise associated with the sampling of replicates from the GP. In the manual's section on GPs, the very last paragraph mentions notes that "A pure logistic Gaussian process regression would not include a noise term in the definition of the covariance matrix This can be implemented by simply removing the noise term(s) sigma_sq from the definition of Sigma.", so I presumed it would similarly be possible to eliminate it here. However, when I do so (by removing the fudge variable altogether), the model takes forever to sample for a given requested iteration count and has a very low ESS for the GP parameters. 

Hence my workaround by adding fudge, but even with fudge included, there's still an annoying tradeoff between sampling speed and smoothness of the posterior. Any ideas on what might be done to avoid the tradeoff?

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
